page: OVHcloud t2-le-90 is a dedicated GPU-accelerated cloud instance engineered for parallel processing and machine learning tasks. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 30 dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, running on Intel Xeon 6226R processors clocked at 2.9 GHz. System memory is configured at 90 GB of RAM, equating to an allocation of 3 GB per dedicated core. Hypervisor virtualization is managed by KVM.

Hardware acceleration is delivered by two NVIDIA Volta V100S GPUs providing a cumulative 64 GB of VRAM. For local IO operations, the host includes a bundled 500 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 4 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires explicit networking considerations during architectural provisioning.

Benchmark measurements position the host as a high-performing execution environment for large language model workloads. In LLM prompt processing, the dual V100S setup achieves top-tier results across small (17,320.17 tokens/sec), medium 7B (1,423.03 tokens/sec), and large 70B parameter models (151.96 tokens/sec). Text generation throughput remains in the upper deciles, reaching 131.54 tokens/sec on 7B models and 18.65 tokens/sec on 70B models. Conversely, CPU-bound operations such as PassMark integer calculations, Geekbench single-core (1245.0) and multi-core (10696.0) scores, and general memory bandwidth register squarely within average performance bands, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression representing an isolated compute highlight.

Given its resource balance, the instance provides balanced cost efficiency for GPU-bound model inference, deep learning model evaluation, and accelerated scientific simulations. Workloads that rely predominantly on general-purpose CPU processing or extensive local file storage will observe diminished return against the specialized Volta accelerator capacity.

Configured on KVM virtualization, it pairs 90 GB of system memory with dual NVIDIA Volta V100S GPUs delivering 64 GB of total VRAM. Storage is supplied via a 500 GB NVMe SSD, and networking operates at a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth. In benchmark testing, the platform exhibits top-tier performance in LLM prompt ingestion and text generation across small, medium, and 70B parameter models, while standard CPU and memory bandwidth benchmarks perform within average ranges. Multi-threaded data decompression is strong, leveraging the dedicated core density. The instance serves workloads centered around deep learning inference, distributed neural network acceleration, parallel batch computing, and GPU-driven technical simulations.
